title: Interteam Sequencing Chronograph: visual dependency timelines and handoff triggers
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Teams routinely miss subtle timing constraints (security review windows, infra provisioning lead time, design handoff freeze) which causes last-minute rework and rollout delays. Goal: Build a lightweight, consumable "Chronograph" view in the Console and Roadmap exports that visualizes sequencing windows, mandatory gating events (security review, infra checklist, design signoff), and automated handoff triggers across Eng/Design/Security/Infra. The Chronograph is not a replacement for the dependency register; it is an orchestration layer that surfaces timing collisions, suggests sequencing fixes, and auto-generates follow-up tickets when a gating event slips. Scope: 1) UI mockups and export formats (CSV/JSON) 2) Mapping rules for gating events and slack windows 3) Integration points with Linear (ticket status changes), GitHub PRs, and Security review tracker 4) Alerting rules and suggested remediation actions. Out of scope: full schedule optimization engine (future phase).
acceptance_criteria: Chronograph Wireframe approved by Design and PM and added to Figma page
Backend mapping service can ingest a small dependency payload (<=50 items) and compute sequence conflicts within 2s
Console shows timeline with gating badges (Security Review, Infra Provisioning, Design Freeze) and hover details
Auto-generated follow-up Linear tickets are created when a gating date moves past the configured slack window
Documented runbook for oncall and release managers describing how Chronograph alerts are triaged

risk_assessment: Medium risk: Mis-specified gating fields could generate noisy alerts. Mitigations: default to Draft auto-tickets, sample payload validation, and conservative slack windows. Longer-term: add trust score and manual review step before enforcement.
implementation_notes: Mapping rules: prefer explicit gating dates (security_review_deadline) over derived estimates. For infra provisioning, use 'infra_request_created' and 'infra_ready_by' pair. Design freeze uses 'design_finalized' + 'freeze_date'. Handoff triggers are Linear state transitions (e.g., 'Ready for Security Review' -> create gating event).
qa_plan: QA will run a 10-project smoke test covering: overlapping gating events, gated ticket slip, auto-ticket draft creation, UI hover details. Create test data set and automated checks in CI.
